name: AdminSDHolder Abuse (SDProp Persistence)
description: Modify AdminSDHolder DACL to include a controlled user. SDProp propagates this ACL to all protected accounts (DA, EA, Administrators) every 60 minutes.

steps.label: Wait for SDProp or force it
Verify ACL propagated to DA group

notes: SDProp runs every 60 minutes by default. Propagates rights to DA, EA, Schema Admins, Administrators, Account Operators, Server Operators.

defense.why_it_works: AdminSDHolder is a special AD container (CN=AdminSDHolder,CN=System,DC=...) whose DACL is used as a template for protected groups (DA, EA, BA, etc.). Every 60 minutes, the SDProp process copies AdminSDHolder's DACL to all members of protected groups, overwriting any custom ACEs. An attacker who adds their account to AdminSDHolder's DACL (with Full Control) will receive that right on every DA account every hour — including after the DA password is changed — creating durable persistence.
defense.prerequisites: Domain Admin rights (to modify AdminSDHolder DACL). PowerView or AD ACL manipulation. A backdoor account to receive Full Control.
defense.impact: T1098 Account Manipulation. Persistent GenericAll over all protected group members, refreshed every 60 minutes. Allows password reset of any DA account indefinitely. Survives DA membership changes — anyone who joins DA in the future also gets compromised.
defense.detection:
Event 5136 on CN=AdminSDHolder,CN=System,DC=... when its DACL is modified. MDI: 'AdminSDHolder modification'. Regular audit of AdminSDHolder DACL for non-default ACEs: Get-ObjectAcl 'CN=AdminSDHolder,CN=System,DC=corp,DC=local'. Downstream: Event 4738 (user account changed) when SDProp propagates and resets DA DACLs.
Account attribute changes (password set, group membership, servicePrincipalName, logon hours) correlated with unusual process lineage or timing (DET0096/AN0265).
Use of usermod, passwd, groupmod on Linux to escalate permissions or persist access on existing users (AN0266).
Modifications to user accounts via dscl, pwpolicy, or sysadminctl on macOS that alter groups, enable root, or bypass MDM (AN0267).
Modifications to SSO/SAML user attributes (isAdmin, role, MFA bypass) through CLI, API, or rogue IdP apps (AN0268).
Addition of new users or role permission changes via API or vSphere Client from non-jumpbox IPs (AN0269).
defense.artifacts: Event 5136: AdminSDHolder DACL modified | MDI: AdminSDHolder abuse alert | Get-ObjectAcl output showing non-default ACE on AdminSDHolder | Event 4738 bulk: many user accounts' DACLs updated simultaneously (SDProp signature)
defense.prevention:
Monitor AdminSDHolder DACL changes (Event 5136 on that specific object). SIEM alert on ANY non-default ACE added to AdminSDHolder. Regular audit: Get-ObjectAcl 'CN=AdminSDHolder,...' and compare to known-good baseline. MDI deployment. Remove non-default ACEs immediately upon detection.
Disable or Remove Feature or Program: Remove unnecessary authentication/authorization mechanisms.
Multi-factor Authentication: Use MFA for all user and privileged accounts.
Network Segmentation: Configure firewalls to limit access to critical systems and domain controllers; use VPCs in cloud environments.
Operating System Configuration: Protect DCs with security config limiting SMB and other unnecessary protocols.
Privileged Account Management: Do not use domain admin accounts for day-to-day operations on unprivileged systems.
Restrict File and Directory Permissions: Restrict access to files dealing with authentication/authorization.
User Account Management: Ensure low-privileged users cannot modify accounts or account-related policies.
defense.evasion: The backdoor ACE only becomes effective after the next SDProp cycle (default 60 min). Make the AdminSDHolder change, wait for propagation, then remove the initial ACE to reduce evidence. Use a subtle ACE (Write Property rather than Full Control) to avoid obvious alerting.
defense.misconfiguration: No monitoring of AdminSDHolder DACL. No SIEM alert on CN=AdminSDHolder modifications. SDProp interval not adjusted (60 min window for detection and response).
defense.vulnerable_config:
# No audit on AdminSDHolder:
# DS Access auditing not enabled → Event 5136 not generated

# AdminSDHolder DACL with backdoor ACE:
Get-ObjectAcl 'CN=AdminSDHolder,CN=System,DC=corp,DC=local' -ResolveGUIDs | Where-Object {
  $_.IdentityReference -match 'backdoor_account'
}
# Output: backdoor_account — GenericAll — propagates to ALL protected group members in 60 min
defense.secure_config:
# Audit AdminSDHolder specifically:
# Enable DS Access → Event 5136, then:
# SIEM: EventID=5136 AND ObjectDN='CN=AdminSDHolder,CN=System,DC=corp,DC=local' → CRITICAL ALERT

# Baseline and monitor AdminSDHolder DACL:
$base = Get-ObjectAcl 'CN=AdminSDHolder,CN=System,DC=corp,DC=local' -ResolveGUIDs
# Save $base to file; run daily comparison:
$current = Get-ObjectAcl 'CN=AdminSDHolder,CN=System,DC=corp,DC=local' -ResolveGUIDs
Compare-Object $base $current -Property IdentityReference,ActiveDirectoryRights
# Any addition → INCIDENT RESPONSE

# Reduce SDProp interval (reduces window for ACE to take effect):
# HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\NTDS\Parameters
# AdminSDProtectFrequency = 300  (5 minutes instead of 60)
